kind: design/pre-build checkpoint (AGENT_CONTRACT section 1: CP1 design, CP2 pilot; FAN-DEPTH 0, so no sub-agent deliverable is being reviewed and both checkpoints are filed by the lane itself)
question: Which branch turns an atom reason of "no district" / "not onboarded" into `no-zoning-stamp`, and what must it do instead where the payload's own zoning facet holds a district and a setback table exists?
answer:
The branch is the FIRST branch of the envelope decision tree in apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts (`if (absenceKind === "no-zoning-stamp")` before this lane; `if (noDistrictBasis && !hasDistrict)` after it). It reads ONE input — the zoning fact's `absence.kind` — and it fires before `hasDistrict`, before the chain setback rule, before the codified table lookup, and before anything the payload's record-composed zoning facet could contribute. A chain in this class therefore can never reach the P-249 `envelope-unverified` branch, no matter what district and table the same payload carries: the envelope status is decided one branch too early, and `facetsNeedLiveEnvelopeDerive` (live-envelope-augment.ts, which requires `envelope.status === "ok"` plus real setback scalars) is never allowed to fire, so no polygon is fetched and the panel draws nothing. Measured live on the XD-2 parcel at this checkpoint's close snapshot: the deployed panel still returns `facets.envelope = {"status":"declined","declineReason":"no-zoning-stamp"}` while the SAME response carries `facets.zoning = {"district":"R-1B","jurisdictionKey":"waco-tx"}` served by the parcel record (`readPath: record`) — the panel declines a district it is itself printing.

The class is a STAMP GAP, not a zoning absence, and the engine says so in its own words (evidence below). So the branch must instead ask the payload-level question the class never asked: is there a district anywhere in this payload and a complete setback table to model an inset from? Where yes, the envelope takes the P-249 branch unchanged (status "ok" so the live derive draws, `figureWithheld: true`, disclosure naming the unverified atom) with the record as the declared source of the scalars. Where no, the decline stands at `no-zoning-stamp` and the atom's own sentence is served unchanged. No district is ever derived, inferred or invented by the adapter: the only district this lane may use is the one the payload already serves in its zoning facet.

reasonList.note: Dispatch step 4: every reason string that reaches the `no-zoning-stamp` decline today, and whether it is a genuine absence. Each member is machine-readable in the code as NO_DISTRICT_DECLINE_SOURCES (atom-chain-to-facets.ts:1944), and the test asserts that every member routes the predicate AND that every member declares `genuineAbsence: false` (atom-chain-to-facets.test.ts, "requirement 5").
reasonList.verdict: No input in this class proves the parcel has no zoning, so none is a genuine absence, and a district the payload already holds contradicts every one of them. The genuine-absence question is answered by the PAYLOAD (no district anywhere in it), never by any of these strings — which is exactly the test the rebuilt branch applies.

design.oneBranch: The decline branch keeps its position in the tree and changes only its guard: `noDistrictBasis && !hasDistrict` instead of `absenceKind === "no-zoning-stamp"`. A new sibling branch handles the stamped gap: `noDistrictBasis && recordDistrict` -> the P-249 branch shape (complete primary-axis table) or `setback-rule-pending` (district, no served table).
design.oneBranchShape: `envelopeUnverifiedBranch()` is the single definition of the drawn-with-figure-withheld shape, used by both the P-249 branch and the stamped-gap branch so the two cannot drift on status/declineReason/figureWithheld; the P-249 disclosure string is byte-identical to the one that branch has served since P-249 (the panel's card and the share brief print it verbatim).
design.neverInvent: `recordDistrict` is read from the payload's own record-composed zoning facet, only for a class member whose chain has no district of its own; a chain with its own district is untouched (test), and a chain outside the class is untouched (test).
design.sourceDeclaration: `setbackSource: "parcel-record"` on the envelope marks the one branch whose scalars came from the record, so the record overlay does not claim the un-overridden axes are atom-chain-sourced on an envelope with no atom-chain axis left.
design.oneRecordRead: pe-property-atoms.ts makes the one record read BEFORE the adaptation, passes it to the adapter and reuses the same result in applyRecordPatch; the read is charged only when the chain passes the adapter's usability gate, so the adapt-failed path pays no read it cannot use.
design.testPlan: Encode the live XD-2 chain and the record stamp; pin falsifier 1 (drawn + withheld + atom named + the live derive fires), falsifier 2 (no district anywhere -> no draw, no invented district, the atom's own sentence served), the partial table, the second cascade code, the untouched own-district chain, and the inventory predicate. Then extend the SHARED fixture's divergence test to run every declared case through the decline branch, without editing the fixture or its casesSha256.

fixtureQuestion.why: The fixture's `not-onboarded` case already declares this atom UNVERIFIED; what was missing was the test's REACH, not the fixture's coverage. The divergence test only ever asked the verification predicate, so no case ran through the decline branch at all. The new cases therefore assert routing over the existing set: only the two stamp-gap cases may be re-routed by a record stamp, and with no district in the payload every case still declines with nothing drawn. Adding a case would also mean editing LDT's byte-identical copy and its casesSha256, which this lane does not do.
